title: Balanced K-flat model for a derived tensor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ and $R'$ be commutative $R$-algebras, and let $M$ be a complex of $A$-modules, viewed on the one-point ringed site and in the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $P\to M$ is a K-flat resolution in $A$-modules and $F\to R'$ is a K-flat resolution in $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], then the total complex $P\otimes_R F$ represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ in the derived category of $A$-modules. Multiplication by elements of $R'$ gives commuting endomorphisms in that derived category and hence an $A\otimes_R R'$-module structure on cohomology. The construction is independent of the chosen resolutions up to the canonical isomorphism in the derived category and is functorial in $M$.

source.place: Tags 064K and 06Y6 (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism, lemma-derived-base-change), balanced derived tensor via K-flat resolutions

proof.text: Regard each commutative ring as the sheaf of rings on the one-point site. Applying [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to the complex M over A (and, after restriction of scalars, to R' over R) supplies K-flat resolutions $P\to M$ and $F\to R'$. The hypotheses already specify such P and F, so the chosen resolutions fit the one-point specialization of the K-flat definitions.

source.place: Tags 064K and 06Y6, existence and choice of K-flat resolutions

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to the ring map $R\to A$ and the complex $N=M$ of $A$-modules: by its clause (2) with $E=R'$, the derived tensor $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ (the value $R'\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M$ of that functor, the factors written in the other order) is represented in $D(A)$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R M)$, the total complex of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] on the one-point site, with $A$ acting through $M$. By its clause (3) for the quasi-isomorphism $u:P\to M$ of complexes of $A$-modules, $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u):\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R P)\to\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R M)$ is an $A$-linear quasi-isomorphism. The symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on $F^p\otimes_R P^q$ is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R F)$. Hence $P\otimes_R F$ represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ in $D(A)$, with $A$ acting through $P$.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) with N=M and E=R', and lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side

proof.text: For $b\in R'$, multiplication $\mu_b:R'\to R'$ is an $R$-linear map, hence an endomorphism of $R'$ in $D(R)$, and $b\mapsto\mu_b$ is a ring map $R'\to\operatorname{End}_{D(R)}(R')$. The functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M:D(R)\to D(A)$ of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2) sends it to a ring map $R'\to\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')$. For $a\in A$, multiplication by $a$ is a morphism $M\to M$ of complexes of $A$-modules ($A$ is commutative), and clause (3) gives the induced natural transformation, represented on the model of Step 2 by multiplication by $a$ on $P$; its naturality with respect to $\mu_b$ says that the endomorphisms induced by $a$ and by $b$ commute in $D(A)$. Applying $H^i$ gives commuting actions of $A$ and $R'$ on every cohomology module, agreeing on $R$, hence an $A\otimes_R R'$-module structure.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, functoriality of the derived tensor in both variables

proof.text: Independence of $F$ is the canonical-comparison part of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2); independence of $P$ holds because for two K-flat resolutions $P\to M$, $P'\to M$ Step 2 gives quasi-isomorphisms from both models to $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R M)$ (up to the symmetry isomorphism), whence a canonical isomorphism in $D(A)$, compatible with a third choice. Functoriality in $M$: a morphism $M\to M'$ of complexes of $A$-modules induces by clause (3) a morphism $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M'\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ compatible with composition, an isomorphism when $M\to M'$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so the construction descends to $D(A)$. The comparison isomorphisms and these morphisms commute with the actions of Step 3 by naturality of the functor and of the transformations of clause (3), so the $A\otimes_R R'$-module structures on cohomology are canonical.
